prompt.provenance_instruction: Answer the following question about Drosophila neuroscience. For every claim you make, state where the information comes from - for example: the specific database, dataset, or tool query you used; the publication (with full citation); or your general training knowledge. If you are uncertain or do not have a source, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004952 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, with different structures at different life stages. Virtual Fly Brain holds extensive data on the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, parts of the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, with over 22,000 images available.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells, including alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes. This information comes from the VFB database, as summarized in the neuron taxonomy. Specifically, the VFB database mentions that there are three main subtypes that project their axons to the gamma lobe, the alpha and beta lobes, and the alpha' and beta' lobes, as referenced by Lee et al., 1999, and Aso et al., 2014. Additionally, VFB holds specific data on gamma Kenyon cells, including images, subclasses, expression patterns, scRNAseq data, and transgene expression, with [3](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of gamma Kenyon cell") images, [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of gamma Kenyon cell") subclasses, [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping gamma Kenyon cell") overlapping expression patterns, [6](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for gamma Kenyon cell") scRNAseq datasets, and 23 transgene expressions available.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, which are known to feed reward or punishment information into the mushroom body. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. VFB holds a range of data related to adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, including images, subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and both downstream and upstream connectivity classes, with thousands of records available across these categories.

results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: The primary neurotransmitter used by [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") Kenyon cells is acetylcholine. This information comes from the VFB database, which supports Kenyon cells as cholinergic, i.e., using acetylcholine, based on VFB neurotransmitter tags, as determined by the VFB query.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which states that any antennal lobe projection neuron sends synaptic output to the mushroom body and/or lateral horn, specifically targeting the mushroom body calyx and lateral horn.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila central brain contains approximately more than 125,000 neurons, according to the Virtual Fly Brain database, as retrieved from VFB. Additionally, VFB holds data on the [adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047885 "Open adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047885,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell") subclasses and [3](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047885,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult central brain astrocyte-like glial cell") records of transgene expression in this cell type.

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
The main components of the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004913 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge, as stated in the VFB database. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the adult central complex, including [1](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of adult central complex") image, information on [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") neurons with some part in the adult central complex, and details on [68](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of adult central complex") parts of the adult central complex. The database also contains information on neurons with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals in the adult central complex, with [362](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex"), [209](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in adult central complex"), and [208](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in adult central complex") records respectively. Additionally, there are [12](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating adult central complex") records of tracts/nerves innervating the adult central complex, [16](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,LineageClonesIn "Run in VFB: Lineage clones found in adult central complex") lineage clones found in the adult central complex, [13,781](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in adult central complex") images of neurons with some part in the adult central complex, and [86](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult central complex") records of transgene expression in the adult central complex.

The literature suggests that these components are associated with a range of functions, including spatial memory, visual navigation, and locomotor control, as discussed in papers such as (Hanesch et al., 1989; Strauss, 2002; Wolff et al., 2015), however, the specific functions associated with each component are not stated in the provided VFB data.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron. Its cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. LPLC2 has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. This arrangement allows it to detect looming stimuli. LPLC2 is involved in detecting looming stimuli and eliciting a jump escape response. It connects to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, specifically from the term info and neuron profile summary for LPLC2, which cites publications by Wu et al., 2016, and Klapoetke et al., 2017.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
The pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain") involves intermediate neuron types, specifically antennal lobe projection neurons. According to the literature, as supported by VFB, the high-level pathway is: [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> adult lateral horn. This indicates that olfactory receptor neurons first transmit signals to antennal lobe projection neurons, which then send axons to higher brain centers, including the adult lateral horn. 

VFB holds extensive data on both olfactory receptor neurons and the adult lateral horn, including images, subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neurons, as well as detailed neuronal and lineage information for the adult lateral horn. Specifically, there are [19014](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of olfactory receptor neuron") images of olfactory receptor neuron, [92](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of olfactory receptor neuron") subclasses, and [575](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") downstream connectivity classes, among other data. For the adult lateral horn, VFB contains [4](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of adult lateral horn") images, information on [1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") neurons with some part in this region, and details on transgene expression and lineage clones. 

This information can be used to further explore the specific connections and neuron types involved in the pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the adult lateral horn.
